notes: arsenal/media/cut.py: trim to the exact frame. copy (snap to the keyframe at or before start, lossless), smart (re-encode only the head up to the next keyframe with hevc_amf/h264_amf at CQP 18, copy the rest bit for bit, one Annex-B stream piped into the muxer, no intermediate files), exact (re-encode the range; GPU lock when estimated over 30 s). Every audio track is kept with an explicit title. plan() is the trim handles' cost preview: median 0.5 ms on a cached keyframe list, 0.9-1.4 s the first time a file is seen. Measured on the 33-min 1080p60 OBS recording: 601.5-612.0 s smart = 630 frames, 0 decode errors, head PSNR 50.8 dB, 470/470 copied frames bit-identical, 1.07-1.23 s; copy 0.10-0.12 s; audio within 1 ms of the source, an MPEG-TS with a 1.4 s format start included (every -ss subtracts the format start_time). verify() picks frames by their own pts, so it cannot share a seek error with the cut; outputs over 1800 frames are decoded and compared on head and tail samples (a 120 s copy verifies in 2.9 s); plan() reports verify_est_s next to est_s. concat() joins parts with the concat demuxer and refuses mismatched codec parameters. py -m arsenal.media cut <src> <start> <end> [out] [--mode smart] [--plan].
